tools.name: start_session
tools.description: Call this first, once per conversation. Returns a session id that every other tool needs. No personal data is required and none is asked for.

tools.name: find_shoe
tools.description: Identifies a shoe one answer at a time. Call it with no answers to get the list of brands, then again with each answer appended: brand, then model, then colourway, then size. It replies with the next question and the answers allowed, until the shoe is identified. Append each option's id, not the nam

tools.name: add_shoe
tools.description: Records a shoe the person owns and the size they wear in it. This is what every recommendation is built from, so ask for at least one shoe that fits them well before calling recommend_size. Use find_shoe first to get the identifiers.

tools.name: list_shoes
tools.description: Shows what the person has told us they own, with the id needed to remove one or to record how it fits.

tools.name: remove_shoe
tools.description: Removes a shoe the person no longer wants counted, using the id from list_shoes. Anything they said about how it fits goes with it.

tools.name: set_foot_measurement
tools.description: Records the length of the person's foot in millimetres, heel to longest toe. More precise than a shoe they own, and worth asking for when they have no shoes to give or the answer matters. A measurement and owned shoes can both be present.

tools.name: rate_fit
tools.description: Records what the person says about wearing a shoe they own: whether it is the right length and width. This is the most valuable thing they can tell us, because it is the difference between what the chart says and what happened. Use the shoe id from list_shoes.

tools.name: recommend_size
tools.description: Works out which size to buy in a shoe the person does not own yet, from the shoes they do own and any foot measurement. Needs at least one owned shoe or a measurement first. Returns the size and what it was based on.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "add_shoe" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.
